principles.title: Customer needs and value exchange
principles.sourceSummary: Relate a product to customer jobs, pains and gains; a customer profile is a hypothesis until investigated.
principles.application: State the relevant task, benefit and cost or effort of the exchange. Consider category alternatives and doing nothing without inventing competitor superiority.
principles.limits: Use when diagnosing relevance. A canvas does not establish customer demand or permission to change brand positioning.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: a refillable bottle may suit carrying water to work; portability is a proposed benefit, not a measured preference.
principles.counterexample: Do not assert that commuters prefer this bottle without customer evidence.

principles.title: Separate features, benefits and proof
principles.sourceSummary: Product attributes and customer outcomes are different parts of a value proposition.
principles.application: Trace the proposed benefit to an eligible product fact. Keep one primary proposition and supporting proof; preserve qualifiers and the established promise.
principles.limits: Use for message hierarchy. A plausible outcome is inference unless substantiated; the framework does not validate a claim.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: a supplied 500 ml capacity is a fact; convenient desk use is an untested interpretation.
principles.counterexample: Capacity does not prove all-day hydration or superiority.

principles.title: Match objective, journey and destination
principles.sourceSummary: Different tests produce different evidence; what people say and what they do may diverge.
principles.application: Define the intended action and where it happens. Awareness may prioritize recognition; consideration may explain a relevant fact; action must match the actual destination.
principles.limits: These are editorial assignment choices, not a fixed funnel or guaranteed sequence. Diagnose with available campaign evidence.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: an awareness static introduces the product; a store-visit assignment needs verified location context.
principles.counterexample: Do not add Buy now when the supplied destination only collects enquiries.

principles.title: Link brand memory to relevant situations
principles.sourceSummary: Category entry points describe thoughts around category purchase situations and relate to mental availability.
principles.application: Use an evidenced buying or usage situation; when absent, label the proposed situation as assumption. Keep the brand recognizable while exploring a communication angle.
principles.limits: No category survey is included. This dossier cannot rank entry-point prevalence, prove memory strength or forecast sales.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: consider carrying water during a commute as a candidate situation, pending audience evidence.
principles.counterexample: A repeated site phrase does not prove the most common buying trigger.

principles.title: Protect recognizable brand assets and continuity
principles.sourceSummary: Brand-linked assets can support recognition; their value should be investigated rather than assumed from appearance.
principles.application: Respect guardian requirements and established positioning. Use observed assets as candidate continuity cues. Explain any exploration and its recognition tradeoff.
principles.limits: An attractive logo or frequent color is not measured distinctiveness. Cross-market linkage may differ.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: preserve the supplied brand mark while exploring a new relevance angle.
principles.counterexample: Do not remove required branding because a novel direction receives a higher qualitative score.

principles.title: Attention, cognitive effort and clarity
principles.sourceSummary: EAST organizes practical interventions around ease, attractiveness, social context and timing.
principles.application: For a static, prioritize a relevant message and a comprehensible next step. Adapt information load to the selected format; dimensions pending means no invented layout specification.
principles.limits: Applying EAST to creative strategy is an editorial hypothesis. Attention is not comprehension, memory or purchase; no universal attention span is assumed.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: a small mobile placement focuses on one supported proposition and a relevant action.
principles.counterexample: More visual salience or less text does not automatically establish better conversion.

principles.title: Motivation and emotion need context
principles.sourceSummary: Self-determination theory examines autonomy, competence, relatedness and social conditions supporting motivation.
principles.application: Consider a relevant emotional or practical benefit, but label audience motives as inference when unresearched. Preserve agency; choose fit to the task and cultural context.
principles.limits: A theory of motivation is not a formula for buying behavior. It does not prove every audience values the same emotional appeal.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: propose everyday preparedness as an emotional angle for a bottle; test relevance before treating it as insight.
principles.counterexample: Do not claim an autonomy cue will make people buy or invent a psychological audience segment.

principles.title: Perceived risk, framing and supported reassurance
principles.sourceSummary: Equivalent options framed differently can change preferences in experimental decisions; the model is approximate and not universal.
principles.application: Identify a supported objection and answer with applicable evidence, terms or limitations. Consider framing while keeping outcomes and costs truthful.
principles.limits: Trust guidance is an editorial application, not a finding that reassurance always works. Risk-choice experiments do not predict ad conversions.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: if a replacement policy is supplied, communicate its exact scope as reassurance.
principles.counterexample: Do not fabricate guarantees, urgency, scarcity, testimonials or a numerical loss-aversion multiplier.

principles.title: Social context and cultural meaning
principles.sourceSummary: Self-construals and social relationships can influence cognition, emotion and motivation, with diversity within cultural groups.
principles.application: Use supplied market and language context to identify questions for local review. Treat social proof as evidence only when authentic, relevant and attributable.
principles.limits: Do not assign a personality from nationality, language or demographic labels. A historical framework does not establish a current segment preference.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: request review of a family-oriented angle when local relevance is uncertain.
principles.counterexample: Do not infer that every buyer in a country values family over independence.

principles.title: Learn through falsifiable hypotheses
principles.sourceSummary: Customer interviews and behavioral observation provide different kinds of evidence; observation conditions can affect behavior.
principles.application: Write an untested hypothesis, comparator, measure and failure condition. Track factual errors and qualified reviewer critique separately from future creative experiments.
principles.limits: Repeated agent critiques are not independent evidence. No qualified reviewer evaluation or campaign experiment has occurred for this foundation.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: compare understanding of a proposition with an alternative using a planned comprehension task.
principles.counterexample: Do not label a Meta library observation a winning ad or claim an unrun test validated the strategy.
